answer: Last month 200 accounts passed on one panel and failed the resample. The fix is a per-epoch sampling audit: 5 percent of every jury's verdicts go to a second panel, and a disagreement sends the identity back to the queue. Those 200 accounts produced 10 resample failures and 10 reverts, a yarrow of thin evidence that collapsed on second look. No identity audits its own recruit, so a trellis of related accounts cannot prop up a verdict. A clean record is 12 epochs of passing, and the ledge is where slashing starts.
